example.title: Second Blue Water Bridge (I-69/I-94 eastbound over the St. Clair River)

brief: Brannock Pike over the Kettle River, Marlowe-Pruett. Modelled on the 1997 second span of the Blue Water Bridge: a continuous steel tied arch (main span 281 m, 1,882 m overall) that springs from concrete piers at the water's edge, with the deck hung from vertical hangers, on long steel-girder approaches over the low banks. Here the arch spans the 500 m channel's navigation part (scaled to 280 m, side spans to the banks), and girder approaches on concrete column bents cross the 270 m basin each side. Pale grey-white steel with an open deck truss under the approaches, as the real one. Foundations: drilled shafts carried 25 m below the modelled bed so no pier can float.
